title: What is known about 1RB---_0RC0LF_1LD0RE_1RC0LB_1RD1RA_1LB0LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_0RC0LF_1LD0RE_1RC0LB_1RD1RA_1LB0LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of numbers: runs (001)^(2j) separated by single 0001. The bouncer side writes the same list in the complemented words 110 / 1110. The recoding sweeps are proved in Lean (six crossing rules). In the samples, a cycle adds 2 to every entry and pushes new small entries at the left end. How the cycle starts and ends is not proved, so halting (A reading a 1) is not ruled out.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,620 cells have been visited and 24,044 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.187). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.5).

claims.title: Recoding sweeps
claims.text: E> (001)^n → (110)^n E>, D> (010)^n → (101)^n D>, C> (100)^n → (011)^n C>, A> (0001)^n → (1101)^n A>, E> (1000)^n → (1110)^n E> and leftward (0111)^n C> 0 → C> 0 (0001)^n, for every n.

claims.title: Every entry +2
claims.text: Write the tape at B's visits to the left end as a list of the lengths of the 001 runs. Between steps 7,203,647 and 8,576,224 the list 8, 4 (7 times), 8, 6, 6, 6, 10, 8, 8, 8, 8, 6, 8, 10, 10, 8, 10, 8, 22, 12, ... becomes 4, 2, then 10, 6 (7 times), 10, 8, 8, 8, 12, 10, 10, 10, 10, 8, 10, 12, 12, 10, 12, 10, 24, 14, ...: every entry is up by exactly 2, and two new entries came in at the left.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.40×10<sup>9</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 1.40×109 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 4 checkpoints, the last at 1.00×109 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 61 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only when A reads a 1. A is entered from E on a 1 (writing 1, moving right), at a run boundary. The samples never show it, but the start and end of a cycle are not proved. CTL (windows of 2 to 5 cells) and NGramCPS (widths 2 to 8, history, LRU) fail.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_0RB0LF_1RA1RE_1RC---_1LC0LB up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_1LB1LF_0LA0RE_1RD0RA_1LD--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: The recoding of whole runs by E, D, C, A.
No halt in the C simulator; 37,620 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.00×10<sup>9</sup> steps).

sections.heading: A list written in two codes
html:
With a = 001 and b = 0001, the tape at a visit of B to the left end reads (step 7,203,647, abridged):

a b^2 a^8 b a^4 b a^4 b a^4 b a^4 b a^4 b a^4 b a^4 b a^8 b a^6 b a^6 b a^6 b a^10 b a^8 ...

That is a list of even numbers (8, 4, 4, ..., 8, 6, 6, 6, 10, 8, ...). A sweep to the right rewrites every word as its complement (001 → 110, 0001 → 1110), a whole run at once (proved in Lean), and the sweep to the left rewrites it back. The right end of the tape is the bouncer, which grows like the square root of the step count:

1 0 (1110)^30 (110)^4 1110 (110)^2 1110 (110)^2 ... C>

sections.heading: All counters tick together
html:
Comparing two samples about 1.4·106 steps apart, every entry of the list has grown by exactly 2, and two new entries (4 and 2) have appeared at the left:

7,203,647:        8  4 4 4 4 4 4 4  8  6  6  6 10  8 8 8 8  6  8 10 10  8 10  8 22 12
8,576,224:  4  2 10  6 6 6 6 6 6 6 10  8  8  8 12 10 10 10 10  8 10 12 12 10 12 10 24 14

So the left side holds a growing list of counters that all advance together. Its length grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted 0.187). From time to time the run b^k at the front changes length and entries are merged at the left end. These events are where the list is reshaped.

What halting would need. A reading a 1 at a run boundary. Proving non-halting would mean proving one full cycle as a rule on the list (all entries +2), and the left-end events as rules on the first entries.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.187). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.5).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,620 cells (512 left of the start, 27,023 right), with a density of 1s of 0.639.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_0RB0LF_1RA1RE_1RC---_1LC0LB: rename A→E, B→C, C→B, D→A, E→D, F→F; it is this table started in state D
  • 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_1LB1LF_0LA0RE_1RD0RA_1LD---: rename A→F, B→D, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→E and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror

summary: A list of counters: the tape is runs of 001 (even lengths) separated by 0001, recoded into 110/1110 and back by every sweep; over a cycle every entry grows by 2 and new small entries are pushed at the left.
family: list of counters, all incremented together
